transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess… it’s my eating that finally made me think I should come in. It’s probably not a huge thing, but my appetite has been kind of all over the place for months. Sometimes I just skip dinner and I’ve lost some weight without really trying, and then other nights I’ll just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking for just myself feels… pointless, I guess. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I mean… maybe a little? I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I’ve just felt kind of flat and not very myself lately. But I know everyone has stretches like that, so I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.
Did something significant change in your life around the time your appetite started to change?

I suppose… yes. It seemed to start around when my divorce was finalized. That was about a year and seven months ago now. I don’t want to blame everything on that, but the timing does line up, I guess.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not trying to lose weight or avoid gaining it. It’s more like… I just don’t feel that interested in food sometimes. I hope that makes sense.
Have you been feeling this flat most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d say most of the day, nearly every day… that sounds so definitive. It’s more that I notice it on and off, like I’m not quite myself. Some days are better than others. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself still feeling upset about the divorce?

I mean… yes, I suppose I do, though I try not to dwell on it. It’s less that I’m crying about it all the time and more that I keep replaying the marriage in my head. I find myself thinking I must have failed at something really basic, even though I know, rationally, relationships are more complicated than that. Does that make sense?
Do you feel that the divorce is still the main reason you’ve been feeling this way?

I’m not completely sure. I think the divorce is part of it, yes, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s the main reason. I don’t want to overstate it. It’s just… it’s there in the background, and I guess I’m trying to understand how much of what I’m feeling is connected to that. Does that answer your question?
Have these feelings been making it hard for you to function in your day-to-day life?

A little, yes. I mean, I’m still getting to work, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely fallen apart or anything. But I’ve noticed my documentation piling up more than it used to, and then I end up staying late to catch up on things that I used to manage pretty easily.

And outside of work… I guess I’ve let things get very small. I don’t see friends much, and even basic routines have kind of slipped. I’m functioning, but not really in the way I normally would, if that makes sense.
Did these changes in your appetite and mood start within about three months after your divorce was finalized?

Yes… I think so. It’s a little hard to pin down exactly, but it really started after the divorce was finalized. That was about a year and seven months ago now. I suppose it’s been going on since then, more or less.
Are you still going through a divorce-related stressor now, or has the divorce itself been over for a while?

The divorce itself has been over for a while. It was finalized about a year and seven months ago. I guess that’s the part I’m trying to explain — it’s not an active divorce process now, but this has sort of been going on since then. Does that make sense?
About how much weight have you lost since this started?

I haven’t kept exact track, which I know I probably should have. It’s not dramatic, but I’ve lost some weight without really trying.

My appetite has just been really inconsistent for months. There are stretches where I’ll skip dinner, and then other nights I’ll just sort of pick at crackers or cereal because cooking for myself feels… pointless, I guess. So I don’t know the exact number, but it has been enough that I noticed.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I mean, I still do things, so it’s not like I’ve completely stopped everything. I water the garden sometimes, and I’ll show up to book club because I don’t want to seem rude or let people down.

But if I’m being honest, it mostly feels kind of flat. I don’t get the same enjoyment out of it. Sometimes I leave early, or I just don’t start the thing at all. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
For at least two weeks at a time, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless nearly every day?

I’m… not sure I’d say hopeless nearly every day for two full weeks. Down, yes, off and on, but I don’t want to overstate it.

There have definitely been periods where most days felt pretty low, but I guess I’m not totally sure how to judge “nearly every day.” Like, I still manage to get through things, so I don’t know if that counts the way you mean.
Have you had any new physical symptoms, like nausea, stomach pain, trouble swallowing, diarrhea, or anything else in your body that seemed to change around the time your appetite went down?

Not that I’ve really noticed, no. I don’t think I’ve had nausea or stomach pain or anything like that.

It’s more just… I’m not hungry, or food feels like too much effort. But physically, I can’t think of a new symptom that started around the same time. Is that okay to say?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

A little, yes. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’ve noticed at work during case reviews I’ll have to reread the same notes several times before they really sink in.

And even small decisions can feel weirdly hard—like which client call to return first, or what to buy for dinner. It takes me longer than it should, which is… embarrassing to admit. Does that count as trouble concentrating?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I’m still showing up and doing what I need to do, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely unable to function.

But even on days when my caseload isn’t unusually heavy, I feel like I’m sort of dragging myself through the hospital. And then when I get home, I’m too tired to do basic things like cook, stretch, or even answer personal messages. It feels a little silly saying that, but… yes, I guess my energy has been pretty low.
Have you been sleeping more or less than usual lately?

A bit less, I think. I can usually get myself into bed at a reasonable time, so it’s not like I’m staying up all night on purpose.

But I’ve been waking up around four in the morning, and then my mind just starts going—bills, work notes I didn’t finish, things with the divorce. I’ll lie there feeling exhausted, but I don’t really fall back asleep before the alarm. Is that the kind of sleep change you mean?
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of wanting to die?

I… I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. I want to say that clearly.

But… yes, sometimes I catch myself thinking it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. And I feel awful even saying that out loud. It scares me, honestly, because if one of my clients said that to me, I know I’d take it seriously. So… I guess I should too, right?
